coverage.assessment: Two setups lose their links. 'She seized hurriedly on the first name' is cut, which removes the alias step. The demure pose loses its 'meek little kid' payoff. 'On the contrary' (first draft) lacks the offer it contradicts.
'The ground glass door' arrives with no building, floor or firm legend. The exit down the stairs is cut, so the scene jumps from office to street clock. Opening pronouns are otherwise clear.

The £100 offer is unattributed and follows a Tuppence action paragraph. 'And the nature of the work?' now answers no mention of work. The bluff climax compresses Whittington's turns, dropping Tuppence's tacit 'I shouldn't like to contradict you'.
£100 offer, £50 paid, three months, ward, secrecy and 'possibly' all survive. The truthful bluffs keep their exact wording.
The narration never explains Whittington's reaction. Brown is not singled out, the pensionnat's purpose is not disclosed, and 'not the faintest comprehension' preserves her limited knowledge.

Signature lines survive, but several narratorial asides go. These include 'proved I have some wits', 'Whittington had scored', the night-before thrill, the stair-top elation and Tommy's astonished eyes. The comic timing thins toward the punchline.

The 'meek little kid... just enough brains for my purpose' line and 'Knew all the time what I wanted you for' are cut. These subtle impersonation hints echoed V2 and prepared Ch. V's pensionnat theory.

Dependencies 0 to 2 are intact on both ends. In dependency 3 the partner 004 revision drops 'You're not going to put that thing in after all?'. In dependency 4 the partner 028 revision drops the 'Esthonia' diary entry. Both local endpoints survive.

strengths: All eight verbatim lines (V1–V8) survive intact, including the turning-point 'Jane Finn' sentence and the five-pound-note closer.

The truthful-bluff sequence ('Rita knows nothing about me', 'Very little indeed', 'It might be my own name', 'by chance') keeps its escalating rhythm and the narratorial 'intoxicated with the success of truthfulness'.
The Brown/telephone-message beat stays neutral and unemphasised, preserving Carter's later deduction.
The telegram keeps Tommy's retained pencil and the ninepence-versus-five-shillings calculation, and the meagre-breakfast motive for 'how much do you want' survives.
summary: The revision keeps the planned skeleton and all eight verbatim lines. The Rita, Brown, telephone-message and £50 mechanics remain intact and unexplained. Further compression in the office scene introduces one genuinely confusing turn: the £100 offer is unattributed and the 'work' it answers no longer exists. It also strips several connective beats: the alias logic, the tacit-admission climax of the bluff, and the 'meek little kid' payoff to Tuppence's demure pose. The office arrival now leans on an undefined 'ground glass door'. Two partner endpoints, in 004 and 028, are missing in their own revisions; neither is a local defect.
